turns: Tell me about basic education in Sokoto State.
reply:
🧭 A broad question: I'm planning the analysis…
---
📚 Reading 7 documents: budgets and budget reports, surveys and statistics, partner reports, plans, financial statements… (up to 3 minutes)
---
✍️ Writing the summary from 25 checked figures…
---
In 2023/2024, public pre-primary and primary schools had 8,284 usable classrooms (Sokoto State Annual School Census 23-24 Report, p. 92), with 2,511 in need of major repairs (30% of usable classrooms) and gaps of 5,170 classrooms with insufficient seating and 3,546 without a blackboard.
For pre-primary and primary education, there were 3,806 teachers in total in 2022, of whom 3,583 were qualified (94%) (Education Sector 2025-2027 Medium-Term Sector Strategy (MTSS), p. 37), against a plan target of 3,836 teachers by 2027 and a target of 11,697 usable classrooms by 2027.
The State Universal Basic Education Board's approved budget was ₦9.11 billion in 2025 (Sokoto State Government 2025 Approved Budget, p. 12) and ₦10.73 billion in 2026 (Sokoto State FY 2026 Budget, p. 18), which was 9.1% of the state's education allocation in 2026, calculated from the budget documents (Sokoto State FY 2026 Budget, p. 32), while actual spending was 39.3% of the final budget in 2023, 89.9% in 2024 (Budget Performance Report Q4 2024, p. 19) and 47.7% in 2025 (Budget Implementation Report Q4 2025, p. 18).
For enrolment and learning in 2021, 53.2% of children of primary school age were out of school and the adjusted net attendance rate was 44.2% (Nigeria 2021 Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS) and National…, p. 298), and for lower secondary school age 46.8% were out of school with an adjusted net attendance rate of 14.1% (Nigeria 2021 Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS) and National…, p. 300).
The education sector plan proposed ₦2.29 billion thousand for the Basic Education Programme in 2025 (Education Sector 2025-2027 Medium-Term Sector Strategy (MTSS), p. 13) and ₦1.05 billion thousand in 2026.
---
[image] 2,511
[1] Sokoto State Annual School Census 23-24 Report, page 92
---
[image] 3,806
[2] Education Sector 2025-2027 Medium-Term Sector Strategy (MTSS), page 37
---
*schools and classrooms*
In 2023/2024, public pre-primary and primary schools statewide had 8,284 usable classrooms (Sokoto State Annual School Census 23-24 Report, p. 92).
Against this stock, 2,511 classrooms were in need of major repairs, which is 30% of usable classrooms.
Other gaps recorded in the same year were 5,170 classrooms with insufficient seating and 3,546 classrooms without a blackboard.
---
*teachers*
In 2022, the baseline for pre-primary and primary education was 3,806 teachers in total (Education Sector 2025-2027 Medium-Term Sector Strategy (MTSS), p. 37), including 3,583 qualified teachers, representing a qualified-teacher share of 94%.
The plan target for 2027 is 3,836 teachers in total for pre-primary and primary education, which is 30 teachers above the 2022 baseline of 3,806.
---
*funding and spending*
The State Universal Basic Education Board's approved budget was ₦9.11 billion in 2025 (Sokoto State Government 2025 Approved Budget, p. 12) and ₦10.73 billion in 2026 (Sokoto State FY 2026 Budget, p. 18), the latter being 9.1% of the state's education allocation in 2026, calculated from the budget documents (Sokoto State FY 2026 Budget, p. 32).
Actual spending was 39.3% of the final budget in the full year 2023, rising to 89.9% in the full year 2024 (Budget Performance Report Q4 2024, p. 19) and then 47.7% in the full year 2025 (Budget Implementation Report Q4 2025, p. 18).
For 2026, actual spending so far in Q1-Q3 was ₦524.16 million (Budget Implementation Report - 2026 Quarter 3, p. 17) against a revised budget of ₦10.73 billion (Budget Implementation Report Q2 2026, p. 17).
---
*enrolment and learning*
In 2021, among children of primary school age in Sokoto State, 53.2% were out of school (Nigeria 2021 Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS) and National…, p. 298) and the adjusted net attendance rate was 44.2%.
F

turns: Waɗanne gundumomin Ƙaramar Hukumar Tambuwal ne ambaliya ta fi rufewa a 2026?
reply:
*Ambaliya: Ƙaramar Hukumar Tambuwal* — na gwaji

A gundumomin Ƙaramar Hukumar Tambuwal, kashin ƙasar da ruwan ambaliya ya rufe (radar) na 2026 ya tashi daga 0.0% (Tambuwal) zuwa 0.7% (Romo Sarki); matsakaici 0.0%. Mafi yawan ƙasa ƙarƙashin ruwa: Romo Sarki (0.7%), Bagida (0.1%), Sabon Birni (0.0%). Mafi ƙaranci: Tambuwal (0.0%), Sanyinna (0.0%), Jabo-Kagara (0.0%).

A 2026, radar ta ga hekta 110 na Ƙaramar Hukumar Tambuwal ƙarƙashin ruwa a wani lokaci (hekta 75 a gonaki, hekta 30 a fadamar kogi, hekta 4 a sauran ƙasa). Radar ta tauraron ɗan adam ta ga ruwan ambaliya a Ƙaramar Hukumar Tambuwal a kowace damina ta 2015–2026; mafi girma ita ce ta 2024, da hekta 4,060 ƙarƙashin ruwa a wani lokaci (hekta 3,270 a gonaki, hekta 550 a fadamar kogi, hekta 240 a sauran ƙasa). Taswirar UNOSAT ta 5–9 Satumba 2024 da 9–13 Nuwamba 2024, da aka haɗa daga kwanaki da dama, ta nuna hekta 8,040, kuma tana kama yawancin ambaliyar fiye da hotunan radar ɗaya-ɗaya. Radar ba za ta iya tantance kashi 42% na Ƙaramar Hukumar Tambuwal ba (gine-gine, bishiyoyi masu yawa, busasshen yashi); a can, rahotannin ambaliya ne madogara.

Madogara: radar ta Copernicus GFM, UNOSAT, JRC; cikakken bayani a nuna lissafi. Bayani ne kawai, ba gargaɗin ambaliya na hukuma ba.

Kuna so na wata gunduma ko ƙaramar hukuma?
